events.reason: nightmares and flashbacks after military service

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry, return evaluation
Visit date: 02/03/2025

Identification: 35-year-old man with hypertension, known to this clinic from an evaluation one year ago for perfectionism and occupational stress, re-referred by primary care.

Presenting problem: For roughly six months he has had recurring, vivid nightmares in which he relives combat from his time in military service; he often wakes from them panicked. He also has daytime flashbacks. Sleep onset is difficult, and he describes a constant sense of being on guard. Primary care started sertraline three months ago, which he has taken consistently, with only partial relief. He denies suicidal ideation.

Medications: sertraline; antihypertensive per PCP (hydrochlorothiazide). NKDA.
Family history: maternal depression; maternal aunt with generalized anxiety; father hypertensive.
Social: never smoker, light social alcohol, works in finance.

Vital signs within normal limits. Physical examination unremarkable. Mental status: alert, cooperative, anxious affect, linear thought, no psychosis, no suicidal ideation.

Assessment: Post-traumatic stress disorder, combat-related, delayed expression. Underlying obsessive-compulsive personality traits as previously described.

Plan: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Referral for trauma-focused psychotherapy (cognitive processing or prolonged exposure). Follow up in clinic in about six months.

Outpatient Psychiatry
[Sent to PCP in response to records request, August 2025.]

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. No note from psychiatry yet.

Per patient: saw psychiatry 2/3, was told this is PTSD from his deployment. They kept sertraline at 50 and want him in trauma-focused therapy; he has an intake call with a therapist next month. Nightmares a bit less often than in the fall, still most weeks. Sleep onset still slow. No SI.

BP fine on HCTZ, no side effects. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart and lungs unremarkable. No edema. Affect brighter than November.

A/P
- PTSD per psychiatry (by his report; will request their note). Sertraline 50 mg refilled x 3 months.
- HTN, controlled. BMP for potassium on the thiazide.
- Front desk to ask psychiatry for the February note.

documents.title: Records request, psychiatry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the psychiatry clinic for the note from his 2/3/25 appointment, release from last year still valid per their office. Will follow up if not received.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Ethan, the doctor reviewed your blood work from Tuesday. Sodium, potassium and kidney function are all normal. No changes.

documents.title: Stopped the sertraline
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know I quit the sertraline about three weeks ago. Honestly it didn't seem to be doing much for me and I'd rather not be on something that isn't helping. I feel about the same off it. Is that OK?

documents.title: RE: Stopped the sertraline
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. I've taken it off your medication list. Three weeks out, the risk of withdrawal symptoms is mostly past. Please keep your psychiatry follow-up and the therapy intake, and tell them you've stopped it, since they may suggest another approach. If the nightmares or mood get worse, reach out sooner.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry, follow-up visit
Visit date: 07/25/2025

Interval history: Seen here in early 2024 for perfectionism and work stress and in February 2025 for combat-related nightmares and flashbacks. Over the past three months he has felt on edge and irritable, sleeps poorly, and has been short with coworkers over trivial matters. He reports tension headaches and tight, aching muscles. He denies any recent change at work or in his personal circumstances, yet appears anxious and acknowledges being swamped by obligations at home, where he is now the main caregiver for his mother, whose health is failing.

Medications: none (no psychiatric medication at present).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with major depressive disorder, maternal aunt with generalized anxiety disorder, father with hypertension.
Social: never smoker, 1 to 2 drinks per week.

Vitals: BP 140/90, HR 88.
Exam: otherwise within normal limits. Mental status: anxious, tense, cooperative, no suicidal ideation, no psychosis.

Labs: CBC within normal limits; TSH within normal limits; urinalysis normal.

Assessment: Adjustment disorder with anxiety, in the setting of caregiving demands. History of PTSD and obsessive-compulsive personality disorder.

Plan: supportive psychotherapy with emphasis on stress management and caregiver support; no medication started. Follow up as needed.

Outpatient Psychiatry
[Sent to PCP in response to records request, August 2025.]

documents.title: Records request, psychiatry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Still no notes from psychiatry for his February visit (asked in March) and patient says he went back in July. Second request faxed with a fresh signed release, asked for both dates. Spoke with their records clerk, she said 2 weeks.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36M here for yearly exam, fasting.

Both psychiatry notes arrived 8/26 and are reviewed. February: PTSD from combat service, sertraline continued, trauma-focused therapy advised. July: adjustment disorder with anxiety tied to caring for his mother; supportive therapy, no medication. He is off sertraline since spring. He did the therapy intake and has been going every other week, finds it useful. Caregiving is still a lot; he is managing.

HTN on HCTZ 25 mg. BP was 140/90 at the July psychiatry visit; reading here is better.
NKDA. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Clear lungs. Abdomen soft and nontender. Skin intact. No peripheral edema. Neuro grossly normal. Anxious but engaged.
PHQ-9 6, GAD-7 8.

Plan
1. Hypertension: on target in clinic, continue HCTZ. CMP.
2. PTSD, adjustment disorder with anxiety, OCPD: followed by psychiatry and his therapist. Problem list updated from the letters.
3. CBC and lipids.
4. Fall vaccines next month at a nurse visit.
Physical again in a year, BP check in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ethan, all of Tuesday's labs are normal: chemistries, potassium, kidney function, blood counts and cholesterol. Nothing to do. Glad the therapy is helping.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 07/31/2026 12:50 by EMS

CC: unresponsive episode with shaking, witnessed.

HPI: 37-year-old man brought in by ambulance from his workplace. Per the coworker who was with him, he was eating lunch when he abruptly stopped responding and went down to the floor, then had generalized jerking movements lasting around a minute. Afterward he was confused for several minutes. He has no memory of the episode. He denies any heart history and has never had an event like this before.

PMH: hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide. Psychiatric history of work-related perfectionism with excessive checking, combat-related nightmares and flashbacks, and more recent irritability with poor sleep.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father hypertension; mother major depression; maternal aunt generalized anxiety.
SH: never smoker; 1-2 drinks weekly; senior financial analyst.

Vitals on arrival: BP 140/85, HR 78, RR 16.
Exam: Alert and oriented x3, back to baseline. Laceration along the lateral border of the tongue. Otherwise unremarkable, including a nonfocal neurologic examination.

ED course: sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium all within normal limits. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no abnormalities. Observed without recurrence.

Impression: seizure, first episode.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Arrange outpatient neurology follow-up. No driving until cleared by neurology. Return for any further episode.

Emergency Medicine
[Faxed to PCP on request.]

documents.title: ER visit Friday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I ended up in the ER on Friday. I apparently passed out at lunch and had a seizure, my coworker called 911. I don't remember any of it, bit my tongue pretty good. They checked blood work and an EKG which were fine and sent me home. They said to see neurology and not drive until then. Can I come in to see you? Do I need a referral for neurology?

documents.title: RE: ER visit Friday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Ethan, sorry to hear this. The doctor asked us to get you in to go over everything and handle the neurology referral at that visit. The first opening is Wednesday 9/2 at 8:00 am. We are also requesting the ER records so they are here for that appointment. If anything happens again before then, go straight to the ER.

documents.title: RE: ER visit Friday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: 9/2 is fine, I'll get a ride. Thanks.
